where-it-lives-and-how-it-builds.text: The application is its own small Lean project over the unchanged registry model, run on the repository's pinned Lean. Its check mode regenerates the corpus and ledgers, replays every scenario, and proves its own checks can fail: an altered outcome, a dropped ledger row and three mutants of the law must each be noticed.

the-law.text: Booking an insertion needs the controller's signature and the full actual registry identity in the envelope. Termination is booked the same way and keeps the token locked. Updates change only the payload. A fold of any selected bookings goes through the registry's own batch fold, releases deposits for terminated keys, and pays every recipient the sum of what it is owed. Rejects release nothing, and every other spend is refused.

finding-dispositions-review-310-model-00.text: Properties needing consistency now assume a reached world, with obligations that consistency holds at genesis and after every action; the counterexamples over arbitrary worlds stay published. Settlement is bound to the rows actually selected. A wrong registry name or policy is refused at booking. The fold's own mint, burning exactly each released key's token, is now stated.

correspondence-limits-implementation-bou.text: Tips, fees and minimum-output funding are outside the model and never absorb a protected deposit. Retraction admission is not exposed, the hashes are stand-ins, and the destination row of a non-delivering fold remains issue 304's question.

coverage.text: Every statement is bound to a scenario, and each scenario publishes the world after every step. The corpus uses one controller, two keys and fixed amounts, so it exhibits the statements without covering their domains. All statements remain unproved.
